title: Symmetric difference between A and B
description:
Given the sets `A = {19, 22, 24, 20, 25, 26}` and `B = {19, 22, 20, 25, 26, 24, 28, 27}`: What is the symmetric difference between A and B?

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `sym_diff(a, b)`, returning a SORTED list of the elements that are in exactly one of the two sets (not in both).
hints: The symmetric difference keeps elements that belong to only one of the two sets, excluding anything shared by both.
Python has a dedicated operator for this - it's different from both union and intersection.
Use the ^ operator (or a.symmetric_difference(b)) to get the elements unique to each side, then return sorted(result).
expected_behavior: Returns a sorted list of the elements that appear in exactly one of the two sets, excluding elements common to both.

hidden_tests.label: identical sets have no symmetric difference

solution:
def sym_diff(a, b):
    return sorted(a ^ b)
explanation: The ^ operator (equivalently, .symmetric_difference()) returns the elements that belong to exactly one of the two sets - it's the union minus the intersection. Since A here is entirely contained in B, only B's extra elements (27 and 28) remain.
